title: Ang 1203–1230: Guru Arjan's Sarang
hook: the fifth Guru's many midday hymns
tomorrow: whose mother, whose father? why would a Guru ask that?

segments.voice: Yesterday, midday: Sarang began, the hottest hour, the Lord as a support all day and night, and a cold cup handed to anyone. Now the fifth Guru fills the raga.
screen: `MIDDAY: SOMETHING TO LEAN ON.` → `NOW, THE FIFTH GURU.`

segments.voice: The message is typed. Half of it's in capitals. Your thumb is hovering over send, your face is hot, and every word in it is true. That's the moment the hymn is for. From ang 1203, Guru Arjan's Sarang hymns run page after page, and in one of them he gives the Name a temperature. Not bright. Not loud. Cool.
screen: `THE MESSAGE, IN CAPITALS.` → `THUMB OVER SEND.` → `THE NAME HAS A TEMPERATURE.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase, the hymn says: the way of the Lord's Name is cool. Seekers searched the old scriptures and the holy people, and drew it out. Thaandhee, the word is: cool, the way shade is cool at noon, the way a wet cloth is cool on a hot forehead. Put that in the middle of a fight. Anger runs hot; that's not a metaphor anyone has to explain. The Granth doesn't tell you the heat is fake, or that you have no reason. It offers a different temperature to stand in. And notice where this sits: in Sarang, the midday raga, where the sun is highest. The hymn knows exactly how hot it gets. That's why it's useful. Something to tell a friend tonight: you can't argue someone out of being overheated, but you can hand them something cool first, and then talk. The order matters. Cool, then words. Guru Arjan's Sarang keeps returning the mind to the Name, and in this hymn, the Name is the shade you step into before you speak.
screen: `THE NAME'S WAY IS COOL.` · `THAANDHEE: SHADE AT NOON.` · `NOT FAKE. A DIFFERENT TEMPERATURE.` · `COOL FIRST, THEN WORDS.` · then, large: `ARJAN'S SARANG.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes. With each breath out, let a little heat leave: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands. Don't chase the thought you're angry about; just let the temperature drop, one breath at a time. If you pray, you can let the Name ride the breath out. If you'd like, read ang 1204 before you begin.
Ang 1203. Where Guru Arjan's Sarang hymns begin, and one of them calls the way of the Name cool.
Arjan's Sarang: in the hottest hour, the Name runs cool. Step into the shade before you hit send. Day done.
